title: Microsoft Teams: admin list of custom apps that need updates for private and shared channels
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts, manifest guidance, licensing and app-management controls are supported. One minor checklist gap remains: the instruction to synchronize blocked apps in Microsoft 365 admin center has no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: Teams admin center lists custom apps in the tenant that need updates to work in private and shared channels.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to view in Teams Admin Center a list of custom apps in their tenant that need to be updated to work in private and shared channels.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the list helps administrators identify impacted apps.
claims.quote: This experience will help admins identify impacted apps

claims.claim: The roadmap says the list helps administrators understand which apps require developer action.
claims.quote: understand which apps require developer action

claims.claim: The roadmap says the list helps administrators coordinate updates.
claims.quote: coordinate updates so users can continue using custom apps across all supported channel types.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn's Teams admin release notes confirm that the custom-app compatibility list is available.
claims.quote: Admins can now view custom apps in the Teams admin center that need updates to work in private and shared channels, helping them identify apps that require developer action.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the list's layout.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center identify custom apps need updates private shared channels list licensing price meter layout criteria. Opened manage-apps, teams-custom-app-policies-and-settings, build-apps-for-shared-private-channels and teams-admin; no list layout.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document the list's incompatibility criteria or whether it relies on supportsChannelFeatures.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center identify custom apps need updates private shared channels list licensing price meter layout criteria; custom apps incompatible private shared channels admin list supportsChannelFeatures. Read developer, Manage apps and admin release-notes pages; no detection criteria.

claims.claim: Most apps can support shared and private channels with a simple manifest update.
claims.quote: Most apps can support shared and private channels with a simple manifest update.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: In app manifest v1.25 and later, supportsChannelFeatures replaces supportedChannelTypes.
claims.quote: Replace `supportedChannelTypes` with `supportsChannelFeatures` when you update your app manifest to v1.25 or later.

claims.claim: The simple tier1 update applies only when the app does not use channel or team membership to determine message delivery, task assignment or permissions.
claims.quote: If your app doesn't: ... Use channel or team membership to determine message delivery, task assignment, or permissions

claims.claim: The simple tier1 update also requires that the app not access or manage files stored in Teams or SharePoint.
claims.quote: Access or manage files stored in Teams or SharePoint

claims.claim: The simple tier1 update also requires that the app not combine or share data across multiple channels or teams.
claims.quote: Combine or share data across multiple channels or teams

claims.claim: The simple tier1 update also requires that the app not customize the experience based on internal, guest or external users.
claims.quote: Customize experience, based on users (internal, guests, or external members)

claims.claim: An app meeting all four conditions only needs supportsChannelFeatures: tier1 added and verification and testing across channels.
claims.quote: Then, you only need to: 1. Add `supportsChannelFeatures`: `tier1` to your app manifest 2. Verify expected behavior, and test your app across channels

claims.claim: Custom apps are developed within or commissioned for the organisation.
claims.quote: Your organization can commission the creation of custom apps for your org-specific requirements. Custom apps can be developed within your organization or by app developers outside the organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Users may be unable to access custom-app experiences in private and shared channels until the required updates are completed.
claims.quote: If apps are not updated to support private and shared channels, users may be unable to access those app experiences in these channels until the required updates are completed.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends reviewing custom apps used in team and channel scenarios.
claims.quote: Review custom apps used in team and channel scenarios across your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends asking developers to complete the required private/shared-channel updates.
claims.quote: Ask your app developers to complete the required updates for private/shared channel scenarios.

claims.claim: The sources do not state whether the list is on by default for every tenant.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom apps" "private and shared channels" "list" "default". Read roadmap, MC1459131, Manage apps, custom-app management and Teams admin release notes; availability is described, but no explicit default or enablement requirement is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that the list changes the behaviour of existing apps when nobody acts.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom apps" "private and shared channels" "list" "default"; custom apps incompatible private shared channels admin list enable disable. Read roadmap, notice, admin release notes and developer guide; no automatic change to existing apps by the list is described.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new data access introduced by the list.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center custom apps private shared channels list 569019 supportsChannelFeatures. Read roadmap, MC1459131, Manage apps and Teams admin release notes; they describe viewing affected apps, not new data access.

claims.claim: The developer page warns that failing to account for channel membership, storage and privacy can cause unintended data exposure.
claims.quote: Ensure that you understand how different channels determine app functionality, membership, storage, or privacy. Otherwise, you might encounter broken functionality or unintended data exposure:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Private and shared channels have their own SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Unlike standard channels, which share a SharePoint site with the team, private and shared channels have their own SharePoint sites.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Channel members can include guests and cross-tenant users.
claims.quote: Channel members might include in-tenant users, guests, or cross-tenant users (external users from other tenants).

claims.claim: Apps that distinguish users to manage access, visibility or feature availability must validate user roles and tenant IDs before granting permissions.
claims.quote: If your app needs to distinguish between various users to manage access, data visibility, and feature availability, then you must validate user roles and tenant IDs before granting permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The list is described as a view, with no automatic action on apps described.
claims.quote: Searched: custom apps incompatible private shared channels admin list PowerShell Graph API enable disable default supportsChannelFeatures. Read roadmap, MC1459131, Manage apps and Teams admin release notes; they describe a view and developer action, not automatic app changes.

claims.claim: Apps already published with an earlier manifest version continue to work.
claims.quote: Apps already published with an earlier app manifest version continue to work.

claims.claim: A manifest declaring supportedChannelTypes cannot be uploaded or submitted under v1.25 and later.
claims.quote: In app manifest v1.25 and later, use `supportsChannelFeatures` instead of `supportedChannelTypes`. If your app manifest declares `supportedChannelTypes`, you can't upload or submit your app.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each organisational user needs a Teams license to use Teams except for anonymously joining meetings.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the existing Teams product entitlement, with no separately published requirement for the list.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to this admin list beyond the Teams licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom apps" "private and shared channels" "list" "license" "price"; Teams admin center identify custom apps need updates private shared channels list licensing price meter. Read user-access, Manage apps, custom-app management and admin release notes; no list-specific licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Manage apps page names the Teams Administrator role as required to use Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for the list at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center identify custom apps need updates private shared channels list licensing price meter; "custom apps" "private and shared channels" "list" "license" "price". Read user-access, Manage apps, custom-app management and admin release notes; no meter for the list.

claims.claim: The developer page gives no price or estimate for update work.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom apps" "private and shared channels" "list" "license" "price". Read build-apps-for-shared-private-channels in full; it describes manifest changes and testing but gives no price or work estimate.

claims.claim: Message extension-only apps operating exclusively in personal scope do not require updates to be available in shared and private channels.
claims.quote: Message extension–only apps that operate exclusively in personal scope do not require updates to be available for users in Shared and Private channels.

claims.claim: The app's details page provides developer support information that administrators can use to contact its developer.
claims.quote: For direct support requests and inquiry about agent or app updates, contact the app developer at their website address available at the following two places: ... App details page of the app in Manage apps page in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The developer page's test guidance covers standard, private and shared channels.
claims.quote: Test your app in a standard channel, a private channel, and a shared channel.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block allows or blocks the selected app.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> changes the app's tenant state through MicrosoftTeams PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. ... Type: Boolean

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Allow or Block is an existing general app-availability control, not a channel-support manifest update; blocked-app settings must remain synchronized between both admin centers until unified app management migration.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no scripting surface for the custom-app compatibility list.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom apps" "private and shared channels" "list" "PowerShell" "Graph"; custom apps incompatible private shared channels admin list PowerShell Graph API. Read Get-AllM365TeamsApps, Update-M365TeamsApp, developer guide and Graph enabledApps excerpt; none exposes the compatibility list.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no admin switch for the list at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: custom apps incompatible private shared channels admin list PowerShell Graph API enable disable default supportsChannelFeatures; "custom apps" "private and shared channels" "list" "default". Read Manage apps, custom-app management, developer guide and admin release notes; no list switch.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to synchronize blocked-app settings under Integrated apps in Microsoft 365 admin center, but the controls table has no row for that surface.
claims.quote: keep blocked-app settings synchronized in Teams admin center and under Integrated apps in Microsoft 365 admin center. ... controls[1].ui.surface: Teams admin center
claims.fix: The After rollout instruction to synchronize blocked-app settings under Integrated apps in Microsoft 365 admin center has no corresponding control row. Retain the necessary synchronization qualification; this finding does not request an additional row.
